**What changed:** `NgComponentOutlet` gained a new optional input, `ngComponentOutletEnvironmentInjector?: EnvironmentInjector`, which provides a custom `EnvironmentInjector` for the dynamically-created component. Previously (in 20.0.0) `ngComponentOutletEnvironmentInjector` did not exist and `createComponent` was called without an `environmentInjector`, so the component inherited the default environment injector. In 20.1.0, when `ngComponentOutletEnvironmentInjector` is set it is forwarded as the `environmentInjector` option to `this._viewContainerRef.createComponent(...)`, and changing it triggers recreation of the component instance (`_needToReCreateComponentInstance` checks `changes['ngComponentOutletEnvironmentInjector']`) (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/54764, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/58aedc37d10208ca40c1b1d4468261dd9aba5356).

**Affects:** Applications that use the `NgComponentOutlet` directive (or `*ngComponentOutlet`) and need the dynamically created component to resolve dependencies from a specific `EnvironmentInjector` (for example a child injector from a webpack Module Federation remote module). Applications that do not use the new input are unaffected and need no changes.

**Action:** none (additive feature). To use it, bind a custom `EnvironmentInjector` to `ngComponentOutletEnvironmentInjector`; if the component's dependency resolution relied on the old inherited environment, re-verify the resolved services.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- 20.0.0: no way to specify the component's environment -->
<ng-container *ngComponentOutlet="componentTypeExpression;
                                  injector: injectorExpression;"></ng-container>

<!-- 20.1.0: provide a custom EnvironmentInjector -->
<ng-container *ngComponentOutlet="componentTypeExpression;
                                  injector: injectorExpression;
                                  environmentInjector: envInjectorExpression;"></ng-container>
```

**What changed:** `NgOptimizedImage` (from `@angular/common`) now exposes a `decoding` input, defined as `@Input() decoding?: 'sync' | 'async' | 'auto';` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.1.x/packages/common/src/directives/ng_optimized_image/ng_optimized_image.ts). The directive proxies this binding onto the host `` element via `setHostAttribute('decoding', this.getDecoding())` in `setHostAttributes()` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.1.x/packages/common/src/directives/ng_optimized_image/ng_optimized_image.ts). If no binding is provided, it defaults to `"auto"`, matching native browser behavior; when `priority` is true, the directive automatically sets `decoding="sync"` to help LCP, and the `priority` attribute overrides any `decoding` input value (https://angular.dev/guide/image-optimization). Allowed values are `auto` (browser decides), `async` (decode off the main thread), and `sync` (decode immediately/blocking) (https://angular.dev/guide/image-optimization, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.1.x/packages/common/src/directives/ng_optimized_image/ng_optimized_image.ts). Valid `decoding` values are asserted in dev mode by `assertValidDecodingInput(this)` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.1.x/packages/common/src/directives/ng_optimized_image/ng_optimized_image.ts). **Affects:** all applications using `NgOptimizedImage`. Prior behavior had no directive-level `decoding` control and relied solely on the browser default; with 20.1.0 the directive now writes a `decoding` attribute onto every image (default `auto`, or `sync` for `priority` images). **Action:** required: re-verify rendering/LCP behavior of priority images, which now get an explicit `decoding="sync"` attribute (and non-priority images an explicit `decoding="auto"`). Developers who want `async` decoding for lazy-loaded images can set the `decoding` attribute. Existing templates compile without change because the default matches the prior browser default and introduces no breaking change (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/61905). **Before/after:** ```html ```

**What changed:** The Angular template **symbol builder** in `compiler-cli` (used by the Angular Language Service to resolve symbols, go-to-definition and hover in templates) previously reported **duplicate directive symbols** for elements whose directive has `hostDirectives`. The builder finds variables referring to template AST nodes at specific offsets and resolves them to directives, then resolves each directive's host directives; because host directives are recorded at the *exact same offsets* as their host, each host directive was added once initially and again when host directives were resolved. Commit c439d69 (PR #61240) resolves this by de-duplicating the symbols (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/c439d6938de60cb132f7ae4d305efa5b3d853e36). The fix shipped as part of PR #61240, "Initial language service support for selectorless", in Angular 20.1.0 (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/61240, ).

**Affects:** Internal `@angular/compiler-cli` / language-service behaviour only — template symbol resolution for directives using `hostDirectives`. No application code, template, dependency or build configuration is affected.

**Action:** none

No code or configuration snippet applies: the change is internal to the compiler-cli symbol builder, and no fetched page contains application-level code in an old/new form.

**What changed:** In 20.1.0, `httpResource` (from `@angular/common/http`) gained two new fields on the `HttpResourceRequest` object: `mode` — "The mode of the request, which determines how the request will interact with the browser's security model… can affect things like CORS… and same-origin policies" — and `redirect` — "The redirect mode of the request, which determines how redirects are handled" (https://angular.dev/api/common/http/HttpResourceRequest). Previously `httpResource` "doesn't expose the redirect and mode options from the underlying Fetch API"; exposing them "would allow developers to control cross-origin behavior and redirect handling more explicitly, enabling better compliance with security policies" (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62337). The commit states the options only work "when using `httpResource` with the `withFetch` provider" (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/27b7ec0a6219645a5af07c2d409c34311a458374). Shipped in 20.1.0 (2025-07-09) under `http` as `feat | add mode & redirect for fetch request in httpResource (#62337)` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.1.0/CHANGELOG.md). A companion commit added the same options to `HttpClient` (#62315).

**Affects:** Applications using `httpResource` (with `provideHttpClient(withFetch())`) that want CORS/same-origin (`mode`) or redirect (`redirect`) control; no existing code breaks.

**Action:** none — purely additive optional request fields. Optionally adopt `mode`/`redirect` in `httpResource` request objects when cross-origin or redirect semantics need to be explicit.

**Before/after:**
```ts
// New usage in Angular 20.1 (PR #62337) — requires the withFetch provider
httpResource(() => ({ url: '/api/register', method: 'POST', mode: 'cors', redirect: 'follow' }));
```

**What changed:** Angular 20.1 added a `credentials` option (type `RequestCredentials | undefined`) to `HttpRequestOptions` / `HttpRequestInit`, which `FetchBackend` forwards to the native `fetch` call (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62354, https://angular.dev/api/common/http/HttpRequestOptions). Accepted values are `'omit'`, `'same-origin'` (default), and `'include'`, controlling whether cookies/authorization headers are sent, e.g. with cross-origin CORS requests (https://angular.dev/guide/http/making-requests). For backward compatibility, the legacy `withCredentials` option takes precedence: if `withCredentials: true` is specified, `credentials` is forced to `'include'` regardless of an explicit `credentials` value (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62354, https://angular.dev/guide/http/making-requests). The option only applies to the fetch backend (the default), not `withXhr()`. Note SSR caveat: during SSR on Node.js (Undici-based fetch), `credentials: 'include'` does not automatically forward cookies from the incoming browser request (https://angular.dev/guide/http/making-requests).

**Affects:** Apps using the default fetch backend that want Fetch-API credential control; existing apps using `withCredentials` are unaffected (behaviour preserved).

**Action:** none — purely additive; existing `withCredentials` usage continues to work and can be optionally migrated to `credentials`.

**Before/after:**
```ts
// GET request with credentials included
http.get('/api/user-data', { credentials: 'include' }).subscribe();
```
(https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62354)

**What changed:** A development-mode warning was added to `HttpClient` when both `withCredentials: true` and the `credentials` option are set on a request. This is implemented via the new `RuntimeErrorCode` value `WITH_CREDENTIALS_OVERRIDES_EXPLICIT_CREDENTIALS` (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62383). It supplements the `credentials` option introduced in #62354, which is added to the `HttpRequestInit` interface and passed through `FetchBackend` to the native Fetch API; for backward compatibility, when `req.withCredentials` is `true` the legacy option overrides `credentials` to `'include'` (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62354).

**Affects:** Applications that pass both `withCredentials` and `credentials` options to the same `HttpClient` request (e.g. `http.get(url, { withCredentials: true, credentials: 'include' })`); the warning is logged only in development mode.

**Action:** none. The change is a log warning only. Re-verify HTTP requests that combine `withCredentials` with `credentials`, and consider removing the legacy `withCredentials` where the new `credentials` option is already set.

**Before/after:**
```ts
// New option added by #62354 (HttpRequestInit / FetchBackend):
http.get('/api/user-data', { credentials: 'include' }).subscribe();
```

**What changed:** The Angular service worker `Driver` now listens for the standard `pushsubscriptionchange` event. When this event fires, the driver captures it and broadcasts a `PUSH_SUBSCRIPTION_CHANGE` message from the service worker to all clients (tabs), so the application becomes aware that its push subscription has changed and can react to it. The feature is intentionally gated for feedback because it is “not possible to perform any end-to-end testing” of this event; the `pushsubscriptionchange` event exists in both Blink and Gecko and is supported in the latest Chrome (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/61856, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/6e1df5479967c2c8b0fadf75e9a9f8c33a342245).

**Affects:** Applications that use the Angular service worker for Web Push notifications (`@angular/service-worker`, `SwPush`), specifically those whose push subscription may expire or otherwise change.

**Action:** none — this is additive. Re-verify that clients correctly handle the newly broadcast `PUSH_SUBSCRIPTION_CHANGE` message (e.g., re-subscribe via `SwPush` when notified). Exact client-side API surface for reacting to this message is unclear from the fetched sources.
